learningObjectives: Distinguish interval inclusion, intersection, metric, and measure as separate kinematic structures.
Explain why a bulk point corresponds to a family of geodesics and hence a curve in kinematic space.
Describe the Crofton reconstruction of curve length under its hypotheses.
State the limited sense in which MERA can discretize kinematic space.
definitions: Incidence: the relation that a represented geodesic intersects a bulk point or curve.
Crofton form: a measure on a space of geometric probes used in integral-geometric reconstruction.
Point curve: the family of geodesics passing through one bulk point, represented as a curve in kinematic space.
Inclusion order: the partial order induced by containment of represented intervals.
Kinematic region: a set of kinematic points satisfying a shared incidence or interval property.
Discretization: a finite or combinatorial representation of selected continuum structure, not automatic identity with it.
notebookPrompt: Create a high-level mathematical cinematic titled ‘Geometry on a space of regions.’ Begin with boundary intervals lifted into a Lorentzian kinematic surface. Visually separate inclusion, overlap, adjacency, metric, and measure rather than merging them. Turn one bulk point into the full curve of boundary-anchored geodesics passing through it. Then deform a convex bulk curve and illuminate the region of kinematic points whose geodesics intersect it; show a Crofton integral over that region becoming the curve length under the cited AdS3 assumptions. Pixelate the kinematic surface into a MERA-like tensor network while explicitly labeling the claim as a model-dependent discretization of kinematic space, not simply the bulk itself. Include the negative control that nearby kinematic points represent nearby intervals or geodesics, not necessarily neighboring bulk points.
humanFrame: The viewer should leave with several structures, not one vague idea of geometry. Use persistent color coding for inclusion, incidence, metric, and measure, and state the reconstruction hypotheses on screen.
assessment: Given a family of boundary intervals, identify inclusion and overlap relations, describe the kinematic curve associated with a bulk point, and explain what set is integrated in the Crofton length formula.
